intro: OBJ to 3MF converts 3D models from OBJ to 3MF on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to prepare a Blender model with several parts and materials for colour printing. 3MF is the modern 3D printing format: a ZIP with the model in XML that stores units, several named parts and the colour of each face, opened directly by PrusaSlicer, Bambu Studio, Cura and Windows.

OBJ is the exchange format of Blender, Maya, 3ds Max and almost every viewer: it stores several named parts and, with its MTL file, materials and colours. OBJ does not store units and is taken as millimetres, the usual case; if your model was drawn in centimetres, metres or inches, say so and the conversion turns it into the units you want for the 3MF. You can also apply a scale, for example 0.5 to print the OBJ at half size.

Each face's colours are stored in the 3MF as a colour group, and each part keeps its name, so you can pick each one's filament in the slicer. If the OBJ has several parts, you can keep them separate inside the 3MF when the format allows it, merge them into one mesh or get one file per part in a ZIP.

The geometry is not simplified or repaired: every triangle of the OBJ reaches the 3MF unchanged, with duplicate vertices merged. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, checked before the file is processed. Files are deleted automatically when they expire.
